title: Federal Reserve Board invites public comment on proposal that would allow U.S. banks and credit unions to use intermediaries to transfer funds through the FedNow Service
summary: The Federal Reserve Board issued a proposal on April 8, 2026, seeking public comment on allowing U.S. banks and credit unions to use intermediaries to transfer funds through the FedNow instant payment service. The proposal would expand the current two-party transfer limitation to enable multi-party transactions, potentially facilitating cross-border payments through correspondent banking relationships.
key_points: Fed Reserve proposes allowing U.S. banks and credit unions to use intermediaries for FedNow Service transfers
Current FedNow transfers are limited to two U.S. banks only
Proposed change would enable correspondent banking connections for cross-border payment portions
Comment period is 60 days following Federal Register publication
Board Memo and Federal Register notice are available as supporting documents
FedNow Service is the Federal Reserve's instant payment infrastructure
why_it_matters: This proposal would expand the functionality of the FedNow instant payment network beyond its original two-party design. By enabling intermediary participation, the Fed is opening pathways for correspondent banking relationships and cross-border payment facilitation through the FedNow rails. This represents an evolution in U.S. payment infrastructure that could affect how banks process certain transactions and compete with private-sector instant payment alternatives.
market_structure_context: The FedNow Service is the Federal Reserve's instant payment infrastructure. This proposal would modify the operational framework of FedNow by allowing three or more parties in a transfer (with an intermediary). This is a market plumbing change that could affect payment flows, correspondent banking relationships, and the competitive dynamics between FedNow and private-sector payment networks.
